q1_issues.issue: The Despite atom's second argument is the family ENTITY sk_family_1, not a reified eventuality — the subordinate clause "being in the same language family" was never reified, so the connective relates a state to a thing.
Stimulus is used for Finnish in the reified "related" state, but Stimulus is licensed only for a psych/perception state's object or a perceived event, and "related" is neither.
(Degree hungarian related distantly) anchors the degree on Hungarian alone even though the predicate is mutual, so the modifier attaches asymmetrically to a symmetric relation.

One fact is recorded twice in non-unifying shapes — the binary (Related hungarian finnish) plus a reified `related` state with Experiencer/Stimulus — and the reified state's licensed flat companion (Member hungarian related) is absent.

q2_gaps: A Symmetric-tagged mutual copular predicate that must serve as a connective-atom endpoint or carry a degree modifier ("only distantly related") — the reciprocals section gives only the assert-once + Symmetric-tag form, with no reified-state shape and no role for the second participant.

A concessive with a non-finite gerund subordinate whose subject is the matrix subject ("Despite being in the same language family, ...") — the connective section assumes two independently reifiable clauses.
notes: Related is licensed as the Symmetric-tagged mutual predicate and Despite as a surface concessive head, so neither is an invented head. "The same language family" is well captured by both languages sharing one witness.
